subject: RFP: Audit Evidence Delivery — Preservation, Formats & Sampling Clarifications
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@hightower.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@hightower.com
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP questions — audit record export, retention, sampling

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the RFP materials. A few clarifying questions from our security and e-discovery teams as we map Redwood's deliverables into our procurement doc: 

1) Export formats: can you confirm which formats you support for bulk audit retrieval (NDJSON, Parquet, CSV)? Do you provide schema/versioned manifests for each export?
2) Retention windows: your baseline says configurable up to 7 years — any hard limits or archival tiers beyond that? Can retention be set per-account or per-route?
3) Sampling & on-demand snapshots: we need a documented sampling procedure (random/stable sampling) and a time-range snapshot capability with chain-of-custody and checksums.
4) PII/redaction: what options exist for in-flight redaction vs. post-export redaction? Is there a supported workflow where you hash or tokenise PII deterministically so we can link records without revealing raw attributes?
5) Delivery & encryption: preferred delivery mechanisms (S3 with SSE-KMS, secure FTP, physical handoff) and whether keys can be customer-managed (BYOK).

We appreciate concise answers and any sample manifests or minimal schema files you can attach. Our timelines: vendor selection week of May 22, evidence snapshots may be requested within 30 days of contract.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Senior Procurement Manager
Hightower Financial

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@hightower.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP questions — audit record export, retention, sampling

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Answers below at a high level; attaching our export spec and a minimal NDJSON schema for reference. Happy to walk through over a call if you prefer.

1) Export formats:
- Supported: NDJSON (recommended for event-by-event traceability), Parquet (columnar for analytics), CSV (flat, limited for nested events).
- Every export includes a versioned manifest (manifest_v{n}.json) with schema URL, export timestamp, event count, file checksums (SHA256), and a provenance header with service version and model runtime.

2) Retention windows:
- Platform supports configurable retention windows per-account and per-route. Default retention tiers: 30d, 90d, 1y, 3y, 7y; archival beyond 7y offered via an offline cold-archive contract (we can exchange a separate SOW for 7-12+ year retention).
- Soft-delete + legal-hold: we support preservation flags that override standard TTL for legal holds (retained until explicit release).

3) Sampling & snapshots:
- Sampling: we support deterministic sampling (hash-based stable sample key) and purely random sampling. Sampling parameters are included in the export manifest; seed and algorithm are recorded to ensure reproducibility.
- Snapshots: time-range exports are generated as point-in-time snapshots (consistent read against the audit ledger) with a signed manifest and SHA256 checksums for each shard. Chain-of-custody metadata is included (export requestor, initiating IP, job id).

4) PII/redaction:
- Options: (A) in-platform deterministic tokenisation/hashing (customer-controlled salt allowed), (B) redaction at export time (masking rules by field), (C) raw export to customer-owned encrypted bucket for in-house redaction.
- We support deterministic HMAC-based hashing using a customer-provided key (BYOK) so you can re-link records without storing raw PII in the deliverable.

5) Delivery & encryption:
- Delivery: S3 (preferred) with SSE-KMS (customer-managed CMK supported), secure HTTPS GET with expiring presigned URLs, SFTP to a customer endpoint, or encrypted physical media under escalated contracts.
- Keys: BYOK supported via KMS integration or HSM-backed key references for on-prem deployments.

Attachments: redwood_audit_export_spec_v2.pdf, sample-ndjson-schema.json, evidence-checksum-manifest.csv

Turnaround: standard bulk export SLA 72 hours from request acceptance; expedited 24-hour SLA possible under contract.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks — that all helps. A couple quick follow-ups: 

- Can you share a redaction policy example for the most common PII fields (email, ssn, ip) and a short note on how deterministic hashing affects dedup/re-identification risk?
- For the deterministic sampling, do you store the sample key server-side or is the seed only supplied at export time? Our compliance team prefers that stable samples are reproducible without keeping a long-lived sample list on your side.

If you can attach the manifest example (sanitized) and the short redaction snippet we can close the technical Qs and move to contract review.

Best,
Elena
